scores.evidence: Phase 1 Foundation: "Event schema, Kafka, tokenization, lakehouse, rules engine inline, labels pipeline"
scores.rationale: Phases go roughly substrate → features → model → go-live → advanced, but no proof gating of dependencies beyond exit criteria, and the online store/decision engine are loosely sequenced.

scores.evidence: Phase 1: "Rules live; ≥12 months of labeled history available"
scores.rationale: Phase 1 builds a broad foundation (6–8 weeks) rather than a thin end-to-end production slice; model scoring doesn't reach production until Phase 3.

scores.evidence: "Are you an issuer, acquirer/processor, or merchant? This decides the actions available, the labels, and the liability."
scores.rationale: Assumptions and open questions exist, including build-vs-buy, but there are no irreversible decisions listed with default plus explicit flip conditions.
No ordering within phases by blast radius; items are listed without priority rationale.

scores.evidence: "tokenize the card number (PAN) at the edge and never store CVV or track data."
scores.rationale: Strong PCI tokenization in ingestion/Phase 1, but security is not addressed in later phases (access control, model/rule change control, etc.).

scores.evidence: "System: latency percentiles, timeout and fallback rate, Kafka consumer lag, feature freshness."
scores.rationale: Monitoring is a standalone section and not tied to Phase 1; only shadow-mode comparison appears in phases.

scores.evidence: "Define each feature once and use that definition for both streaming and batch backfill"
scores.rationale: Feature definitions, point-in-time correctness, registry and versioning are covered, but not threaded as per-phase environment/build reproducibility.

scores.evidence: "if features or the model time out, use rules only and a conservative default per segment... use circuit breakers."
scores.rationale: Good fallback design, but in a standalone section and not tied to phase deliverables; load testing isn't phase-scheduled.

scores.evidence: "Later: sequence models ... and graph neural networks (GNNs) in the async path."
scores.rationale: Rules precede the model and shadow mode/champion-challenger exist, plus human analysts, but there are no explicit budgets or defenses, and ML layers are not ordered on the AI-layer sequence.

scores.evidence: "4. Advanced (ongoing) | Graph/ring detection, sequence models, automated retraining, exploration slice | Gains measured per added part"
scores.rationale: Deferred items are listed with a vague measured-gain condition, but no explicit pull-forward triggers.

note: Solid domain content on fraud architecture, but weak on build-plan structure: no thin production slice first, no decision gates with flip conditions, and cross-cutting concerns sit in standalone sections.
